rule.title: AWS Bucket Block Public Access Weakened
rule.author: Shoban Chiddarth

es.summary: Una identidad de AWS ejecutó con éxito PutBucketPublicAccessBlock y desactivó al menos una de las cuatro protecciones de Block Public Access de un bucket S3. Puede ser un paso previo a exponer el bucket mediante una ACL o una bucket policy públicas.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de CloudTrail con eventSource s3.amazonaws.com y eventName PutBucketPublicAccessBlock en los que BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy o RestrictPublicBuckets queda en false, y errorCode es Success o está vacío (la llamada tuvo éxito).
es.why_it_matters: Block Public Access es el control que impide que un bucket se publique por error o de forma maliciosa. Desactivarlo es una forma de debilitar defensas (etiqueta de la regla: T1686.001) y suele anteceder a la exfiltración o exposición de datos.
triage_steps: Identifique el bucket (requestParameters.bucketName), la cuenta y la región, y determine qué flags quedaron en false en PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.
Revise userIdentity: ARN, tipo (IAMUser, AssumedRole, Root), sesión y si se usó MFA. Confirme si la identidad suele administrar S3.
Valide sourceIPAddress y userAgent: consola, CLI, Terraform o SDK desconocido; compare con la actividad habitual de esa identidad.
Busque en +/- 15 minutos PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl, PutObjectAcl o DeleteBucketPolicy sobre el mismo bucket que lo hagan público.
Verifique si también cambió el Block Public Access a nivel de cuenta (PutAccountPublicAccessBlock) o hubo cambios en otros buckets.
Revise la actividad previa de la misma identidad: ConsoleLogin, AssumeRole, CreateAccessKey, GetCallerIdentity, alertas anteriores.
Clasifique la sensibilidad del bucket y busque GetObject/ListObjects desde IPs externas si hay data events habilitados.
Confirme con el dueño del bucket si existe un ticket de cambio aprobado.
false_positives: Administradores que ajustan Block Public Access para un sitio web estático, CDN o distribución pública de archivos aprobada.
Pipelines de infraestructura como código (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) que aplican una configuración definida con flags en false.
Entornos de laboratorio o pruebas donde se configuran buckets públicos de forma intencional.
response_steps: Si el cambio no está autorizado, restaure las cuatro opciones de Block Public Access en true para el bucket y revise el nivel de cuenta.
Elimine ACLs o bucket policies públicas añadidas, conservando una copia de la configuración para la investigación.
Si la identidad parece comprometida, desactive o rote sus access keys, revoque sesiones del rol y fuerce el restablecimiento de credenciales.
Evalúe exposición de datos con logs de acceso al servidor o data events de S3 y escale según la sensibilidad.
Considere una SCP o AWS Config rule que impida o alerte sobre la desactivación de Block Public Access.
es.severity_rationale: Medium porque el cambio debilita un control clave de exposición de datos, pero por sí solo no hace público el bucket y suele tener causas administrativas legítimas.

en.summary: An AWS identity successfully called PutBucketPublicAccessBlock and disabled at least one of the four Block Public Access protections on an S3 bucket. This can precede exposing the bucket through a public ACL or bucket policy.
en.what_it_detects: CloudTrail events with eventSource s3.amazonaws.com and eventName PutBucketPublicAccessBlock where BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy or RestrictPublicBuckets is set to false, and errorCode is Success or empty (the call succeeded).
en.why_it_matters: Block Public Access is the guardrail that prevents a bucket from being made public. Turning it off impairs defenses (rule tag T1686.001) and often comes right before data exposure or exfiltration.
triage_steps: Identify the bucket (requestParameters.bucketName), account and region, and note which PublicAccessBlockConfiguration flags were set to false.
Review userIdentity: ARN, type (IAMUser, AssumedRole, Root), session context and MFA usage. Confirm whether this identity normally manages S3.
Check sourceIPAddress and userAgent: console, CLI, Terraform or an unfamiliar SDK; compare with that identity's usual activity.
Search +/- 15 minutes for PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl, PutObjectAcl or DeleteBucketPolicy on the same bucket that make it public.
Check for account-level changes (PutAccountPublicAccessBlock) or similar changes to other buckets.
Review the identity's earlier activity: ConsoleLogin, AssumeRole, CreateAccessKey, GetCallerIdentity and prior alerts.
Assess bucket data sensitivity and, if data events exist, look for GetObject/ListObjects from external IPs.
Confirm with the bucket owner whether an approved change ticket exists.
false_positives: Administrators adjusting Block Public Access for an approved static website, CDN origin or public file distribution.
Infrastructure-as-code pipelines (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) applying a defined configuration with flags set to false.
Lab or test environments where public buckets are configured on purpose.
response_steps: If unauthorized, set all four Block Public Access options back to true on the bucket and review the account-level setting.
Remove any public ACLs or bucket policies added, keeping a copy of the configuration as evidence.
If the identity looks compromised, disable or rotate its access keys, revoke role sessions and force credential reset.
Assess data exposure using S3 server access logs or data events and escalate based on sensitivity.
Consider an SCP or AWS Config rule that prevents or alerts on disabling Block Public Access.
en.severity_rationale: Medium because the change weakens a key data-exposure control but does not by itself make the bucket public, and legitimate admin changes are common.

positive.description: Assumed role disables BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets on a bucket via CLI; successful call with no errorCode.
IAM user turns off all four Block Public Access flags from the console; errorCode recorded as Success.

negative.description: Terraform re-enables all Block Public Access flags (hardening, no flag set to false).
Attempt to disable BlockPublicAcls is denied, so errorCode is AccessDenied rather than Success or null.
